overall: The AG found the Marblehead Board of Health did not violate the Open Meeting Law by secretly deliberating on a revolving fund request; the authority question was outside the law's scope.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board must have secretly deliberated on a commercial waste revolving fund, since it was not discussed in open session across several meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Absent sufficient evidence to the contrary, we credit the Board’s account of the facts and find that it did not have any private discussions outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint argued that the Board's failure to discuss the revolving fund request showed improper action, but the AG said a body need not discuss any given topic.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to discuss any topic.

allegations.summary: Complaint implied the Director of Public Health effectively made decisions that belonged to the Board as a whole, in sending revolving fund requests to the Select Board.
allegations.key_passage: this allegation goes to the authority of individuals versus the Board to take action on particular matters, which is not a matter governed by the Open Meeting Law.
